When a known device is connected, OTG Master will prompt for your device lock and then mount all recognized encrypted drives automatically. Credentials are stored in AES-256 encrypted form in Android Keystore — they cannot be extracted without your device lock.
Cached credentials invalid for %1$s — cleared. Enter credentials again to re-enable Auto mount.
Opt out of Auto mount for this device
Mount encrypted partitions read-only by default
All Auto mount cached credentials cleared.
%1$s disconnected while mounted. If it drops during transfers, it may need more power than the phone can supply. Try a powered USB hub or an enclosure with its own power supply.
%1$s disconnected while mounted. Check the cable and connections.

The phone was on battery when this drive dropped. The most common cause is power: SSDs and hard drives in bus-powered enclosures can draw more than a phone\'s USB port supplies, especially during long transfers.
The phone was on external power when this drive dropped, so a weak power supply is less likely. Start with the connection.
Use a USB hub with its own power supply: plug the hub into the wall, the drive into the hub, and the hub into the phone.
Or use an enclosure with its own power input.
Use a short, direct USB-C cable. Avoid loose adapters, and make sure each plug is fully seated.
Keep the phone charged. Some phones limit USB power when the battery is low.

If files were being written when it dropped, check the drive on a computer before writing to it again (chkdsk on Windows, fsck.exfat or e2fsck on Linux). An ext4 drive may open read-only until its journal is repaired, which its card offers. Reading it is safe.
Plug the drive back in to mount it again. Its disconnects stay listed on its card until the app closes.
Unplug the drive and plug it back in. When Android asks whether OTG Master may access it, tap Allow.
Connect it with an OTG adapter, or a USB-C drive directly. Some cables only charge and carry no data.
Some phones, including OnePlus, Oppo, Realme and Vivo, read USB drives only while OTG is switched on in Settings (search Settings for \"OTG\"). It switches itself off after a few minutes unused.
Some phones cannot read a drive while charging through the same port. If the drive appears only with the charger unplugged, connect it directly with an OTG adapter.

SSDs and hard drives may need more power than the phone can supply. If the drive\'s light stays off, or it disconnects shortly after appearing, try a USB hub with its own power supply, on a phone that can read drives through one.
Drives locked by their own hardware, such as WD\'s password lock, must be unlocked with the maker\'s software first.
Encryption: VeraCrypt (AES, Serpent, Twofish and their cascades), LUKS1, LUKS2, BitLocker, and encrypted APFS.
File systems: FAT32, exFAT, NTFS and ext4, read and write; APFS, read-only.
Unencrypted drives with these file systems open on their own when plugged in.
Not unmounted cleanly. Read-only until repaired.
This ext4 drive was not unmounted cleanly, so its journal still holds changes that never reached their place on the drive. Until they do, OTG Master opens it read-only.
Repairing replays the journal: it applies those changes, the same way Linux does the next time it mounts the drive. No files are deleted.
If any part of the journal fails its checksum, nothing is changed and the drive stays read-only. Check it on a computer with e2fsck.
%1$s repaired: %2$d journal transaction(s) replayed, %3$d block(s) written. It is writable now.
%1$s was not repaired and stays read-only: %2$s
Drive repaired. It is writable now.
Repair failed. The drive stays read-only. See the log.
%1$d locked partition(s) on %2$s, beside one already mounted.

This phone does not support USB drives (it reports no USB host / OTG support).
This phone\'s USB port is connected to a computer, with the phone as the device, so it cannot read a drive through that port.

This phone is charging through its USB port. Many phones cannot read USB drives while charging that way: if the drive is on a hub with a power supply, unplug the power supply, or connect the drive directly with an OTG adapter.
OTG connection is switched off, so USB drives cannot be seen. Turn it on in Settings (search Settings for \"OTG\"), then plug the drive in again.
On %1$s phones, USB drives work only while OTG is switched on in Settings (search Settings for \"OTG\"). It switches itself off after a few minutes unused.

Drives you unlock or plug in appear here.
Every sector is overwritten. Slower: about a minute per GB over USB.
Only the filesystem structures are written. The old data stays on the drive, readable with recovery tools, until it is overwritten.
Keep the drive attached and the app open until this finishes.
Everything on this partition will be erased.
The new volume stays inside its encrypted container, with the same password, and keeps the partition\'s size. The same filesystem also keeps its cluster size.
The partition keeps its size. The same filesystem also keeps its cluster size.
This erases the partition and creates a new, empty encrypted volume on it. Your current files are not moved into it: copy them somewhere else first.
The PIM must be a number.
Empty for VeraCrypt\'s default (416 MiB, 6 passes). Higher values need more memory and time to unlock.
Keep a copy of every keyfile: the volume cannot be opened without them. Their order does not matter.
Up to 11 characters. Clear it for no label.
All data on %1$s (%2$s) will be cleared. This cannot be undone.
Encrypted (%1$s, %2$s) with %3$s inside. Unlock it now with the password, PIM and keyfiles you chose, to check they open it before you copy anything onto it.
Keep the drive attached until it finishes
Files stay available in other apps until you unmount.
